questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Plants of this group are diploid and well adapted to extreme conditions. They grow bearing sporophylls in compact structures called cones. The group in reference is
questions.explanation: Gymnosperms are diploid sporophytes with xerophytic adaptations such as thick cuticles and sunken stomata. They bear micro- and megasporophylls arranged in compact cones (strobili).
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q6)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The male sex organ of a bryophyte and the gametes it produces are, respectively:
options: Antheridium; non-flagellated male gametes carried by a pollen tube
questions.explanation: In bryophytes the antheridium is the male sex organ, and it produces biflagellate antherozoids that swim through water. Pollen tubes belong to seed plants, and zoospores are asexual spores of algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II for structures in gymnosperms.
List-I
(a) Nucellus
(b) Pollen grain
(c) Megasporophyll
(d) Microsporangium
List-II
(i) Bears ovules and may be clustered into female cones
(ii) Site where pollen grains develop
(iii) Reduced male gametophyte
(iv) Tissue from one of whose cells the megaspore mother cell differentiates
questions.explanation: The megaspore mother cell differentiates from a cell of the nucellus. The pollen grain is the reduced male gametophyte and develops inside the microsporangium, while ovules are borne on megasporophylls.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, roughly what share of the total carbon dioxide fixation on earth is carried out by algae through photosynthesis?
questions.explanation: Algae carry out at least half of the earth's total CO$_2$ fixation. This makes them globally important photosynthesisers, not minor contributors.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A pteridophyte bears small leaves (microphylls) and compact strobili, and it produces two kinds of spores, large and small. Which option correctly identifies the plant and its class?
questions.explanation: Selaginella, a member of Lycopsida, has microphylls, forms strobili and is heterosporous. Equisetum forms strobili but is not heterosporous. Lycopodium shares the class but is not listed as heterosporous. Salvinia is heterosporous but is not described with microphylls and strobili.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A microbiologist prepares a solid culture medium using a commercial product obtained from Gracilaria. Which feature is correctly associated with the class to which this alga belongs?
options: Food is stored as laminarin or mannitol
Chlorophyll a and b dominate, and pyrenoids store starch
Food is stored as floridean starch, and flagellated cells are absent
Asexual reproduction is by pear-shaped biflagellate zoospores
questions.explanation: The product is agar, and Gracilaria is a red alga (Rhodophyceae). Red algae store floridean starch and have no flagella. The other options describe brown algae (options 1 and 4) or green algae (option 2).
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student examines a filamentous green alga during sexual reproduction. She finds that the fusing gametes are flagellated and similar in size. The alga and its mode of sexual reproduction are most likely
questions.explanation: Similar-sized gametes indicate isogamy. Among filamentous forms, Ulothrix has flagellated isogametes, whereas Spirogyra's isogametes are non-flagellated. Eudorina is anisogamous and Volvox is colonial and oogamous.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (genus) with List-II (class of pteridophytes) and choose the correct option.
List-I
(A) Psilotum
(B) Lycopodium
(C) Equisetum
(D) Adiantum
List-II
(I) Sphenopsida
(II) Pteropsida
(III) Psilopsida
(IV) Lycopsida
questions.explanation: The pairings are Psilotum with Psilopsida, Lycopodium (like Selaginella) with Lycopsida, Equisetum with Sphenopsida, and Adiantum (a fern, like Pteris and Dryopteris) with Pteropsida.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Gelidium
B. Sargassum
C. Chlorella
D. Sphagnum
List-II
(i) Source of peat used as fuel and packing material
(ii) Source of agar
(iii) Protein-rich food supplement used by space travellers
(iv) Marine brown alga used as food
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Gelidium yields agar, and Sargassum is among the brown algae eaten as food. Chlorella is a unicellular, protein-rich supplement, and the moss Sphagnum provides peat.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Mosses, along with lichens, are among the first organisms to colonise bare rocks, and they decompose rock to make the substrate suitable for higher plants.
Statement II: Mosses increase soil erosion because their dense mats prevent rainwater from soaking into the soil.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.explanation: Mosses play a pioneer role in succession on rocks along with lichens, so Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because the dense mats of mosses soften the impact of falling rain and prevent soil erosion.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Both gymnosperms and angiosperms produce seeds. Which feature separates angiosperms from gymnosperms?
options: Angiosperms are heterosporous, while gymnosperms are homosporous
In angiosperms the ovules are enclosed and the seeds are covered within fruits, while in gymnosperms the ovules and seeds are exposed
Angiosperms have a dominant sporophyte, while gymnosperms have a dominant gametophyte
Only angiosperms possess xylem and phloem
questions.explanation: Gymnosperm ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall, so their seeds are naked. Angiosperm seeds are enclosed in fruits. Both groups are heterosporous, both have a dominant sporophyte and both have vascular tissues.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The embryo sac of an Angiosperm is made up of
questions.explanation: A typical angiosperm embryo sac contains 3 antipodals, 2 synergids, 1 egg cell and 1 central cell. The central cell holds 2 polar nuclei, giving 7 cells but 8 nuclei.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q7)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about angiosperms is correct?
options: They are divided into two classes, the dicotyledons and the monocotyledons
They are divided into four classes: Psilopsida, Lycopsida, Sphenopsida and Pteropsida
They are restricted to narrow geographical regions because they need water for fertilisation
Their pollen grains and ovules develop in strobili, and their seeds remain naked
questions.explanation: NCERT divides angiosperms into dicotyledons and monocotyledons. The four classes listed belong to pteridophytes. Restricted spread due to water-dependent fertilisation describes pteridophytes, and naked seeds borne on strobili describe gymnosperms.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The main, conspicuous plant body of a bryophyte is:
questions.explanation: The dominant body of a bryophyte is haploid and produces gametes, so it is a gametophyte. In pteridophytes, by contrast, the dominant body is the diploid sporophyte.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student observes a flat, dorsiventral, green thallus of a liverwort. Small cup-like receptacles on its upper surface contain tiny green bodies, and rhizoids are present on its lower surface. Which statement about these tiny green bodies is correct?
options: They are diploid buds formed after fertilisation
They are haploid, multicellular asexual buds that detach and grow into new individuals
They are unicellular spores produced by meiosis in the capsule
They are male sex organs that release biflagellate antherozoids
questions.explanation: The cups are gemma cups, and the bodies inside are gemmae: green, multicellular asexual buds. They arise from the haploid gametophyte, so they are haploid. Meiotic spores form only in the sporophyte's capsule, not on the thallus.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following algae is an example of a colonial form?
questions.explanation: Volvox is the colonial example given in NCERT. Spirogyra and Ulothrix are filamentous, and Laminaria is a large brown alga.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A student describes a marine alga with these features:
- an olive-brown body attached to rocks by a holdfast, with a stalk and a leaf-like photosynthetic frond;
- asexual reproduction by pear-shaped zoospores bearing two unequal, laterally attached flagella.
In what form does this alga most likely store its food?
questions.explanation: A holdfast, stipe and frond together with pyriform zoospores bearing two unequal lateral flagella identify a brown alga (Phaeophyceae), which stores laminarin or mannitol. Floridean starch is the reserve of red algae, and starch in pyrenoids is typical of green algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are correctly attributed to the liverwort Marchantia?
(i) Thallus is dorsiventral
(ii) Thallus is closely appressed to the substrate
(iii) Gemma cups are present on the thallus
(iv) Upright, slender axes bear spirally arranged leaves
(v) A protonema stage develops directly from the spore
(vi) Sporophyte consists of foot, seta and capsule
questions.explanation: Features (i), (ii), (iii) and (vi) belong to Marchantia, giving a total of four. Spirally arranged leaves on upright axes and a protonema stage are features of mosses, not of thalloid liverworts.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The colour of brown algae varies from olive green to various shades of brown. Which pigment determines this variation, depending on how much of it is present?
questions.explanation: The colour of Phaeophyceae depends on the amount of the xanthophyll pigment fucoxanthin. r-Phycoerythrin gives red algae their colour, and chlorophyll b and d are not found in brown algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Pyrenoids are storage bodies found in the chloroplasts of most green algae. What do they contain?
questions.explanation: NCERT states that pyrenoids contain protein besides starch. Oil droplets are a separate food store in some green algae, and floridean starch is the food reserve of red algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The plant body of a typical brown alga is attached to the substratum by a holdfast and has a stalk. What is its leaf-like photosynthetic organ called?
questions.explanation: The plant body of a brown alga is differentiated into a holdfast, a stalk called the stipe, and a leaf-like photosynthetic frond. The stipe is the stalk, not the photosynthetic organ.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following pairs consists only of haploid structures?
options: Gemma of Marchantia and seta of Funaria
Capsule wall of a moss and protonema of a moss
Gemma of Marchantia and protonema of Funaria
Foot of a liverwort sporophyte and spore mother cell
questions.explanation: Gemmae arise from the haploid gametophyte, and the protonema grows from a haploid spore, so both are haploid. The seta, foot and capsule wall belong to the diploid sporophyte, and spore mother cells are diploid because they are the cells that undergo meiosis.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Species of the moss Sphagnum have long been used as packing material for trans-shipment of living material. This use is mainly due to their:
questions.explanation: Sphagnum holds a lot of water, so it keeps living material moist during transport. The same moss also provides peat used as fuel. Algin and agar are algal products.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about systems of plant classification is incorrect?
options: Linnaeus's system was artificial, being based largely on vegetative characters or androecium structure.
Bentham and Hooker's classification of flowering plants was a natural system that also considered internal features.
Numerical taxonomy gives greater weightage to reproductive characters, since vegetative characters are easily affected by environment.
Cytotaxonomy uses information such as chromosome number, structure and behaviour.
questions.explanation: Numerical taxonomy assigns numbers and codes to all observable characters and gives each one equal importance. The idea of weighting characters by how much the environment affects them is the criticism raised against artificial systems, not a feature of numerical taxonomy.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Archegonia occur in three of the following plant groups. Which group does NOT bear archegonia?
questions.explanation: Bryophytes and pteridophytes bear archegonia on their gametophytes. The gymnosperm female gametophyte also bears two or more archegonia. Angiosperms lack archegonia. A common trap is assuming that gymnosperms lack them because they bear seeds.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements comparing gymnosperms with heterosporous pteridophytes such as Selaginella is INCORRECT?
options: Both produce two kinds of spores, microspores and megaspores
In both, the female gametophyte is retained on the parent sporophyte for some period
In gymnosperms, the pollen tube carries the male gametes towards the archegonia, so external water is not needed for their transfer
In gymnosperms, the male gametophyte leads an independent free-living life like the prothallus of ferns
questions.explanation: Unlike pteridophytes, gymnosperm gametophytes have no independent free-living existence. The male gametophyte is the reduced pollen grain, which develops inside the microsporangium and is then carried by air to the ovule. The other statements are correct.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The giant Redwood tree (Sequoia sempervirens) is a/an
questions.explanation: Sequoia, the giant redwood, is a gymnosperm and one of the tallest tree species. It bears naked seeds in cones.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q10)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Members of Chlorophyceae are usually grass green in colour. This is mainly due to the dominance of which pigments?
questions.explanation: Green algae are grass green because chlorophyll a and b dominate, and these pigments are held in definite chloroplasts. Chlorophyll c with fucoxanthin belongs to brown algae, and chlorophyll d belongs to red algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Apart from vegetative characters, the artificial system of classification given by Linnaeus was based mainly on the structure of the:
questions.explanation: Linnaeus's artificial system relied on vegetative characters or on the structure of the androecium. Using so few characters often separated closely related species.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In heterosporous pteridophytes such as Selaginella, the zygote develops into a young embryo within the female gametophyte
In gymnosperms, the multicellular female gametophyte bears two or more archegonia and is retained within the megasporangium
The male gametophyte of gymnosperms is highly reduced to a limited number of cells and is called the pollen grain
In gymnosperms, the megaspore mother cell differentiates from one of the cells of the integument surrounding the nucellus
questions.explanation: The megaspore mother cell arises from one of the cells of the nucellus. The integuments (envelopes) only protect the nucellus to form the ovule. The other statements match NCERT, including retention of the embryo inside the female gametophyte in Selaginella as a precursor to the seed habit.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The sporophyte of a liverwort is differentiated into:
questions.explanation: The liverwort sporophyte has three parts: a foot, a seta and a capsule, and spores form in the capsule after meiosis. Holdfast, stipe and frond describe brown algae, while root, stem and leaves describe the pteridophyte sporophyte.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Artificial systems of classification are not acceptable, partly because they gave equal weightage to vegetative and sexual characteristics.
Reason (R): Vegetative characters are often more easily affected by the environment.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Vegetative characters change more readily with the environment. Giving them the same weight as sexual characters is therefore misleading, so R directly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about gymnosperms are correct?
(i) They are heterosporous and produce haploid microspores and megaspores.
(ii) Pollen grains develop within the microsporangia.
(iii) The female gametophyte is shed from the ovule and lives independently in damp soil.
(iv) The megaspore mother cell divides mitotically to form four megaspores.
(v) Pollen grains are carried by air currents to the opening of the ovules.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (v) are correct. The female gametophyte stays inside the megasporangium, so (iii) is wrong, and the megaspore mother cell divides by meiosis, not mitosis, so (iv) is wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The spread of living pteridophytes is limited and restricted to narrow geographical regions.
Reason (R): Pteridophytes lack xylem and phloem, so they cannot conduct water efficiently.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Pteridophyte spread is limited because their gametophytes need cool, damp, shady places and fertilisation needs water. R is false: pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues, xylem and phloem.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following genera is a member of Rhodophyceae?
questions.explanation: Polysiphonia is a red alga, as are Porphyra, Gracilaria and Gelidium. Dictyota, Ectocarpus and Fucus are all brown algae (Phaeophyceae).
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which group of plants is regarded, in evolutionary terms, as the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues (xylem and phloem)?
questions.explanation: Pteridophytes are the first land plants with xylem and phloem. Bryophytes live on land but lack vascular tissues. Gymnosperms have vascular tissue but evolved later.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In algae, vegetative reproduction occurs by
options: budding of gemmae from gemma cups
fragmentation, in which each fragment grows into a thallus
questions.explanation: Vegetative reproduction in algae is by fragmentation, and each fragment develops into a new thallus. Zoospores belong to asexual reproduction and gamete fusion to sexual reproduction. Gemmae are found in liverworts.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In Pinus, the male and the female cones are borne on the same tree.
Statement II: In Cycas, the male cones and the megasporophylls are borne on different trees.
Choose the correct option.
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Pinus bears both kinds of cones on one plant. Cycas carries male cones and megasporophylls on separate plants, and it has no compact female cone.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
I. In heterosporous pteridophytes, the zygote develops into a young embryo within the female gametophyte retained on the parent sporophyte, which is a precursor to the seed habit.
II. In gymnosperms, the female gametophyte has an independent, free-living existence like the prothallus of ferns.
III. In Cycas, male cones and megasporophylls are borne on the same tree.
IV. In gymnosperms, the megaspore mother cell differentiates from one of the cells of the nucellus.
Which of the statements are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and IV agree with NCERT. In gymnosperms, neither gametophyte is free-living, since both stay within sporangia on the sporophyte, so II is false. Cycas bears male cones and megasporophylls on different trees, unlike Pinus, so III is false.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Cyanobacteria are classified under
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria (blue-green algae) are prokaryotes. Under the five-kingdom classification, all prokaryotes are placed in Kingdom Monera.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q1)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the plant in List-I with the site where meiosis occurs in List-II.
List-I:
(a) Liverwort
(b) Fern
(c) Gymnosperm
(d) Angiosperm
List-II:
(i) Anthers and ovules within flowers
(ii) Capsule of the sporophyte attached to the gametophyte
(iii) Microsporangia and megasporangia borne in cones
(iv) Sporangia borne on the leaves of the free-living sporophyte
questions.explanation: In each group, meiosis occurs in the sporophyte to form spores. The sites differ: the capsule of a liverwort, sporangia on fern leaves, the sporangia of gymnosperm cones and the anthers and ovules of angiosperm flowers.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about heterospory and the seed habit is INCORRECT?
options: In Selaginella, the female gametophyte is retained on the parent sporophyte for variable periods, and the young embryo develops within it
In gymnosperms, the pollen grain is a highly reduced male gametophyte that develops within the microsporangium
In Cycas, male cones and megasporophylls are borne on the same tree, as in Pinus
In gymnosperms, one megaspore develops into a multicellular female gametophyte bearing two or more archegonia
questions.explanation: Pinus bears male and female cones on the same tree, but in Cycas the male cones and megasporophylls are borne on different trees. The other three statements agree with NCERT. Retention of the female gametophyte in heterosporous Selaginella is a precursor to the seed habit.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Holdfast, stipe and frond constitutes the plant body in case of
questions.explanation: In brown algae (Phaeophyceae), the plant body is usually differentiated into a holdfast for attachment, a stalk-like stipe and a leaf-like photosynthetic frond.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q3)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding classification systems is INCORRECT?
options: Phylogenetic systems assume that organisms of the same taxon have a common ancestor
Information from other sources becomes especially important when there is no supporting fossil evidence
Bentham and Hooker's classification is a phylogenetic system based on evolutionary relationships
Artificial systems separated closely related species because they were based on a few characteristics
questions.explanation: NCERT describes Bentham and Hooker's classification as a natural system based on natural affinities, not as a phylogenetic one. The other three statements agree with the text.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which sequence correctly traces the life cycle of a moss from the first cell of the gametophytic generation to the first cell of the next sporophytic generation?
options: Spore mother cell → protonema → leafy stage → zygote
Spore → protonema → leafy stage bearing antheridia and archegonia → zygote
Spore → leafy stage → protonema bearing sex organs → zygote
questions.explanation: The haploid spore is the first cell of the gametophyte. It forms the protonema, which gives rise to the leafy stage that bears the sex organs. Fertilisation then produces the diploid zygote, the first cell of the sporophyte. The spore mother cell is diploid and belongs to the sporophyte, and the capsule is part of the sporophyte rather than its first cell.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (structure) with List-II (its nature).
List-I
A. Protonema of moss
B. Seta of moss
C. Prothallus of fern
D. Pollen grain of Pinus
List-II
(i) Diploid; part of a sporophyte that depends on the gametophyte for nourishment
(ii) Haploid; free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte
(iii) Haploid; highly reduced male gametophyte confined to a few cells
(iv) Haploid; creeping, filamentous stage that develops directly from a spore
Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation: The protonema is the first, filamentous stage of the haploid moss gametophyte. The seta belongs to the diploid sporophyte (foot, seta and capsule), which is attached to and nourished by the gametophyte. The prothallus is the free-living haploid fern gametophyte, and the pollen grain is the reduced male gametophyte of gymnosperms. The trap is assuming that every part of a moss is haploid.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following pteridophytes produces two kinds of spores, microspores and megaspores?
questions.explanation: Salvinia, like Selaginella, is heterosporous. Dryopteris, Pteris and Adiantum are ferns of Pteropsida and are homosporous, like the majority of pteridophytes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Read the following statements about green algae.
Statement I: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of pectose and an outer layer of cellulose.
Statement II: In green algae, the pigments are localised in definite chloroplasts.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: The layers in Statement I are reversed. The inner layer of the green algal cell wall is cellulose and the outer layer is pectose. Statement II is correct, because the pigments are held in definite chloroplasts of varied shapes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct for mosses?
(i) The protonema develops directly from a spore and is creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous.
(ii) Antheridia and archegonia are borne on the protonema.
(iii) Vegetative reproduction occurs by fragmentation and by budding in the secondary protonema.
(iv) The sporophyte is less elaborate than that of liverworts.
(v) Spores are formed in the capsule after meiosis.
(vi) Gemmae formed in gemma cups are their main means of asexual reproduction.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (iii) and (v) are correct. In mosses, sex organs form at the apex of the leafy shoots, not on the protonema, and the moss sporophyte is more elaborate than that of liverworts. Gemma cups are characteristic of liverworts such as Marchantia, not mosses.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In numerical taxonomy, each character is given equal importance.
Statement II: Numerical taxonomy can handle only a few characters at a time, so it is usually done manually.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Numerical taxonomy is now easily carried out on computers and can consider hundreds of characters at once, each given equal importance. Statement II is therefore wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Red algae occur both in well-lighted regions close to the water surface and at great depths in the ocean.
Reason (R): Red algae lack chlorophyll a and depend entirely on r-phycoerythrin for photosynthesis.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: NCERT states that red algae grow near the surface as well as at great depths, so A is true. R is false because Rhodophyceae possess chlorophyll a and d along with r-phycoerythrin.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In bryophytes, the zygote undergoes reduction division immediately after fertilisation to produce haploid spores.
Statement II: In bryophytes, haploid spores are produced by meiosis in some cells of the multicellular sporophyte.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: The bryophyte zygote does not undergo meiosis at once. It first develops into a multicellular sporophyte, and only some cells of that sporophyte undergo meiosis to form spores.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following groups consists only of members of Chlorophyceae?
questions.explanation: Chlamydomonas, Chara and Spirogyra are all green algae. Fucus and Dictyota are brown algae, and Porphyra is a red alga, so each of the other groups contains a non-green member.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following structures in a gymnosperm such as Pinus is haploid?
options: Cells of the female gametophyte that bears the archegonia
questions.explanation: The female gametophyte develops from a haploid megaspore produced by meiosis, so its cells are haploid. The nucellus and megasporophyll belong to the diploid sporophyte, and the embryo comes from the diploid zygote, so it is also diploid.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Cyanobacteria, though called blue green algae, are no longer placed among the algae of Kingdom Plantae.
Statement II: In Spirogyra, the gametes are flagellated and similar in size.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Members of Monera, such as cyanobacteria, have been removed from Plantae, so they are no longer 'algae'. Spirogyra shows isogamy with non-flagellated (non-motile) gametes. Flagellated isogametes are found in Ulothrix.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following genera belongs to Rhodophyceae?
questions.explanation: Gracilaria is a red alga, along with Polysiphonia, Porphyra and Gelidium. Dictyota, Sargassum and Ectocarpus are all brown algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about mosses is incorrect?
options: The protonema develops directly from a spore and is a creeping, green, branched, frequently filamentous stage
The leafy stage develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud
Antheridia and archegonia are produced at the apex of the leafy shoots
The sporophyte of mosses is simpler than that of liverworts and lacks an elaborate spore dispersal mechanism
questions.explanation: NCERT states that the moss sporophyte is more elaborate than the liverwort sporophyte. Mosses also have an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal. The other three statements describe the moss gametophyte correctly.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about members of Chlorophyceae are correct?
(a) Their grass-green colour is due to the dominance of chlorophyll a and b.
(b) Their plant body is always multicellular, either colonial or filamentous.
(c) Asexual reproduction is by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia.
(d) Some members store food in the form of oil droplets.
(e) Their motile cells bear two unequal, laterally inserted flagella.
(f) Their reserve food is floridean starch.
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (c) and (d) are correct, giving 3. Statement (b) is wrong because unicellular forms such as Chlamydomonas also occur. Statement (e) describes brown algae, since green algae have 2-8 equal, apical flagella. Statement (f) describes the reserve food of red algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are included in NCERT's general description of algae?
Chlorophyll-bearing; thalloid body; autotrophic nutrition; largely aquatic; presence of xylem and phloem; differentiation into true root, stem and leaves
questions.explanation: Algae are described as chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic, which makes four features. Vascular tissue and true roots, stems and leaves first appear in pteridophytes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Conifers are able to limit water loss even in conditions of extreme temperature, humidity and wind.
Reason (R): Conifers have needle-like leaves with reduced surface area, a thick cuticle and sunken stomata.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Needle-like leaves reduce the surface area for transpiration, while the thick cuticle and sunken stomata further cut down water loss. These features directly explain why conifers tolerate harsh conditions.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following cells are haploid?
Protonemal cell of a moss; leaf cell of a moss; prothallus cell of a fern; gemma cell of Marchantia; zygote of a fern; meristem cell of a monocot; ovum of a liverwort; primary endosperm nucleus of a dicot
questions.explanation: The protonema, moss leaf, prothallus, gemma and liverwort ovum all belong to the gametophyte, so these five are haploid (n). The fern zygote and monocot meristem cell are diploid (2n), and the primary endosperm nucleus is triploid (3n).
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In most brown algae, asexual reproduction is by pear-shaped zoospores bearing two unequal, laterally attached flagella.
Statement II: Red algae reproduce asexually by non-motile spores.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Brown algae have biflagellate, pyriform zoospores with unequal lateral flagella. Red algae lack flagella entirely, so their spores and gametes are non-motile. Both statements are therefore correct.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Equisetum (horsetail) is placed in which class of pteridophytes?
questions.explanation: Equisetum is the example given for Sphenopsida. Lycopsida includes Selaginella and Lycopodium, Psilopsida includes Psilotum, and Pteropsida includes the ferns.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following is a moss?
questions.explanation: Polytrichum is a moss, like Funaria and Sphagnum. Marchantia is a liverwort, Selaginella is a pteridophyte and Ulothrix is a green alga.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Among the three classes of algae (Chlorophyceae, Phaeophyceae, Rhodophyceae), which of the following characters is found only in Chlorophyceae?
options: Presence of cellulose in the cell wall
Presence of chlorophyll b, with food stored as starch
questions.explanation: Chlorophyll b and true starch are listed only for green algae; brown algae have chlorophyll c and red algae have chlorophyll d and store floridean starch. The other options are shared: cellulose walls and fragmentation occur in all three classes, and oogamy occurs in all three as well (for example Volvox, Fucus and red algae).
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Marchantia, gemmae are best described as:
options: Haploid non-motile spores formed by meiosis inside the capsule
Green, multicellular asexual buds formed in small receptacles on the thallus
Diploid buds formed at the tip of the seta
Flagellated male gametes released from the antheridia
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds that develop in gemma cups on the liverwort thallus. They detach and grow into new plants. They are not spores, because they are not formed by meiosis, and they are not gametes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II for a typical bryophyte:
List-I
(a) Rhizoids
(b) Archegonium
(c) Antheridium
(d) Sporophyte
List-II
(i) Produces biflagellate male gametes
(ii) Some cells undergo meiosis to form haploid spores
(iii) Attach the plant body to the substratum
(iv) Flask-shaped organ producing a single egg
questions.explanation: Rhizoids anchor the plant, the archegonium is flask-shaped with one egg, the antheridium produces biflagellate antherozoids, and the sporophyte forms spores by meiosis. Option 2 is the trap: it swaps the two sex organs.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the economic importance of algae are correct?
(i) At least half of the total carbon dioxide fixation on earth is carried out by algae.
(ii) Algin is a hydrocolloid produced in large amounts by red algae.
(iii) Carrageen is a water-holding substance obtained from red algae.
(iv) Chlorella, a multicellular brown alga, is used as a protein-rich food supplement by space travellers.
(v) Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum are among the 70 species of marine algae used as food.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (iii) and (v) are correct. Algin comes from brown algae, not red algae, so (ii) is wrong. Chlorella is a unicellular alga, not a multicellular brown alga, so (iv) is wrong. The common trap is swapping algin and carrageen between the brown and red algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about bryophytes are correct?
(i) The main plant body is haploid and produces gametes.
(ii) The antheridium produces biflagellate antherozoids.
(iii) The flask-shaped archegonium produces numerous eggs.
(iv) The sex organs are unicellular.
(v) Haploid spores are formed by meiosis in some cells of the sporophyte.
(vi) The plant body is anchored by true roots in the leafy forms.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (ii) and (v) are correct. Statement (iii) is wrong because the archegonium produces a single egg, and (iv) is wrong because the sex organs are multicellular. Statement (vi) is wrong because bryophytes lack true roots and are attached by rhizoids.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Phylogenetic systems of classification, which are accepted at present, are based on:
options: Gross morphological characters such as habit and leaf shape
Only the chemical constituents of plants
Only the number of stamens in a flower
questions.explanation: Phylogenetic systems are based on evolutionary relationships and assume that members of the same taxon share a common ancestor. Superficial morphology was the basis of the earliest artificial systems.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Phaeophyceae is incorrect?
options: They possess chlorophyll a and c along with carotenoids and xanthophylls
Their vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin
Their gametes are pyriform with two laterally attached flagella, and gametic union always takes place in the surrounding water
Besides plastids, their protoplast contains a centrally located vacuole and nucleus
questions.explanation: Brown-algal gametes are indeed pear-shaped with two lateral flagella. However, in oogamous species union of gametes can take place within the oogonium, not only in water, so 'always in water' makes option 3 incorrect.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Sexual reproduction in Spirogyra is described as isogamous even though its gametes are non-motile.
Reason (R): Isogamy refers to the fusion of gametes that are similar in size, whether or not they are flagellated.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: NCERT calls fusion of similar-sized gametes isogamous, whether the gametes are flagellated (Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (Spirogyra). R therefore explains A. Motility is not the criterion for isogamy.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Carrageen is a commercially used hydrocolloid (water-holding substance). Which group of algae produces it in large amounts?
questions.explanation: Carrageen comes from red algae, while algin comes from brown algae. Mixing up these two hydrocolloids is the usual trap.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The prothallus of a pteridophyte is best described as:
options: A diploid, dependent sporophyte attached to the gametophyte
A compact cone of sporophylls bearing sporangia
A haploid, free-living, mostly photosynthetic, thalloid gametophyte
A diploid embryo retained within the female gametophyte
questions.explanation: Spores germinate to form the prothallus. It is a small but multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic, thalloid gametophyte, and it is haploid. It should not be confused with a strobilus, which is a cone of sporophylls.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The most common type of spore produced during asexual reproduction in algae is the
questions.explanation: Algae reproduce asexually by several types of spores. The most common are zoospores, which are flagellated (motile) and germinate into new plants. Conidia are fungal spores, and an oospore forms by sexual fusion.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Pyrenoids are storage bodies found in the chloroplasts of most members of Chlorophyceae. Besides starch, pyrenoids contain:
questions.explanation: In green algae, pyrenoids are located in the chloroplasts and contain protein in addition to starch. Laminarin and mannitol are the stored food of brown algae, and floridean starch is the stored food of red algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Members of Phaeophyceae range in colour from olive green to various shades of brown.
Reason (R): The colour of brown algae depends on the amount of the xanthophyll pigment fucoxanthin present in them.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Brown algae do show shades from olive green to brown. This variation arises from the differing amounts of fucoxanthin masking their chlorophylls a and c, so R correctly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Protonema is
options: Haploid and is found in mosses
Diploid and is found in liverworts
Diploid and is found in pteridophytes
Haploid and is found in pteridophytes
questions.explanation: The protonema is the first stage of the moss gametophyte, a creeping green filamentous structure that develops directly from a spore. Since it arises from a haploid spore, it is haploid.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q9)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Algin
(b) Carrageen
(c) Agar
(d) Chlorella
List-II
(i) Protein-rich food supplement
(ii) Hydrocolloid from red algae
(iii) Hydrocolloid from brown algae
(iv) Used to grow microbes; obtained from Gelidium
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Algin is the brown-algal hydrocolloid and carrageen is the red-algal one. Agar from Gelidium is used for microbial culture, and Chlorella is a protein-rich supplement. Option 1 swaps algin and carrageen.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A plant shows the following features:
(i) a dominant sporophyte with true roots, stem and leaves containing xylem and phloem
(ii) small leaves (microphylls)
(iii) sporophylls grouped into compact strobili
(iv) two kinds of spores, with the female gametophyte retained on the parent sporophyte
(v) no ovules
The plant is most likely:
questions.explanation: Selaginella fits every clue: it is a vascular sporophyte with microphylls and strobili, and it is heterosporous with a retained female gametophyte. Equisetum has strobili but is homosporous. Dryopteris is a homosporous fern with macrophylls. Cycas bears ovules.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Living pteridophytes are restricted to narrow geographical regions.
Reason (R): Their gametophytes need cool, damp, shady places to grow, and water is required for fertilisation.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The prothallus needs cool, damp, shady conditions, and antherozoids need water to reach the archegonium. Together, these requirements limit the spread of pteridophytes, so R directly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Bryophytes are called the amphibians of the plant kingdom.
Reason (R): Bryophytes can live in soil, but they depend on water for sexual reproduction.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Bryophytes live on land, but their antherozoids must swim through water to reach the archegonium. This dual dependence on land and water is exactly why they are called amphibians of the plant kingdom.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about mosses is correct?
options: The leafy stage is anchored by unicellular, unbranched rhizoids
Vegetative reproduction occurs by fragmentation and by budding in the secondary protonema
Antheridia and archegonia are produced at the base of the leafy shoots
The sporophyte is the predominant stage of the life cycle
questions.explanation: Mosses reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation and by budding in the secondary protonema. Their rhizoids are multicellular and branched, and the sex organs form at the apex of the leafy shoots. The gametophyte, not the sporophyte, is the predominant stage.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about pteridophytes is INCORRECT?
options: Sporangia are subtended by leaf-like appendages called sporophylls
Spores are produced by meiosis in spore mother cells within the sporangia
In heterosporous forms, the zygote develops into a young embryo within the female gametophyte, which is considered a precursor to the seed habit
The sporophyte remains attached to the gametophyte and derives nourishment from it throughout its life
questions.explanation: In pteridophytes the sporophyte is the dominant, well-differentiated, independent phase. A dependent sporophyte is a feature of bryophytes. The other three statements are correct according to NCERT.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The natural system of classification for flowering plants, which used internal features as well as external ones, was given by:
options: George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker
questions.explanation: NCERT credits George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker with a natural classification of flowering plants based on natural affinities. Linnaeus gave an artificial system, and Whittaker proposed the five kingdom system for all living organisms.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: If the diploid number of a flowering plant is 36. What would be the chromosome number in its endosperm?
questions.explanation: The endosperm is triploid (3n) because it forms when a male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei. Here n = 18, so 3n = 54.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q8)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
A marine alga has these features:
- No flagellated cell appears at any stage of its life.
- It stores a carbohydrate very similar in structure to amylopectin and glycogen.
- Its cell wall contains polysulphate esters.
Which option correctly identifies a possible genus and a commercial use associated with it?
options: Gelidium – source of agar used to grow microbes
Fucus – oogamous alga with a large non-motile egg, used for agar
questions.explanation: Lacking flagella entirely, storing floridean starch and having polysulphate esters in the wall all point to red algae. Gelidium, a source of agar, fits. Laminaria and Fucus are brown algae with flagellated zoospores or gametes, and Chlamydomonas is a flagellated green alga.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In bryophytes, the sporophyte is not free-living and remains attached to the gametophyte.
Reason (R): In bryophytes, the zygote undergoes reduction division immediately after fertilisation.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The sporophyte depends on the photosynthetic gametophyte for nourishment, so A is true. R is false because the zygote does not undergo meiosis immediately. Instead, it forms a multicellular sporophyte, and only some cells of that sporophyte later undergo meiosis.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly contrasts liverworts with mosses?
options: Liverworts: gametophyte arises from a protonema bearing lateral buds; Mosses: gametophyte grows directly from the spore as a flat thallus
Liverworts: leafy members bear tiny leaf-like appendages in two rows; Mosses: upright axes bear spirally arranged leaves
Liverworts: sporophyte has foot, seta and capsule; Mosses: sporophyte lacks a seta
Liverworts: meiosis occurs inside the gemma cup; Mosses: meiosis occurs inside the antheridium
questions.explanation: Leafy liverworts have leaf-like appendages in two rows, while the moss leafy stage has spirally arranged leaves on upright axes. Option 1 swaps the protonema feature, which belongs to mosses. Both groups have a foot-seta-capsule sporophyte, and meiosis occurs in the capsule in both.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about pteridophytes are correct?
(i) The main plant body is a sporophyte differentiated into true root, stem and leaves.
(ii) Spores are produced by mitosis in spore mother cells.
(iii) The gametophyte is multicellular, free-living and mostly photosynthetic.
(iv) Antherozoids reach the archegonium by air currents.
(v) The zygote develops into a well-differentiated sporophyte, which is the dominant phase.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (iii) and (v) are correct. Statement (ii) is wrong because spores form by meiosis in spore mother cells. Statement (iv) is wrong because water, not air, carries antherozoids to the mouth of the archegonium.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Chlorella is used as a food supplement, even by space travellers. Which property of this alga makes it suitable for this use?
options: It is a large kelp with a massive plant body
It produces carrageen in large amounts
It is a unicellular alga rich in proteins
questions.explanation: Chlorella is a unicellular alga with a high protein content, which is why it serves as a food supplement. Agar and carrageen come from red algae, and kelps are brown algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are haploid?
(i) Protonema of a moss
(ii) Seta of Funaria
(iii) Gemma of Marchantia
(iv) Prothallus of a fern
(v) Pollen grain of Pinus
(vi) Nucellus in an ovule of Cycas
(vii) Female gametophyte of Pinus
(viii) Capsule wall of a liverwort sporophyte
questions.explanation: Five are haploid because they are gametophytic: the protonema, gemma, prothallus, pollen grain (the reduced male gametophyte) and the female gametophyte of Pinus. The seta and capsule wall belong to the diploid sporophyte. The nucellus is diploid megasporangium tissue of the sporophyte.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following algae has a colonial plant body?
questions.explanation: Volvox is the colonial form described in NCERT. Ulothrix and Spirogyra are filamentous, and Laminaria is a kelp-type brown alga with a large plant body.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pair correctly gives the smallest and one of the tallest angiosperms mentioned in NCERT?
questions.explanation: Angiosperms range from the tiny Wolffia to Eucalyptus trees over 100 metres tall. Sequoia is a gymnosperm, and Chlorella is a unicellular alga, so neither can be an example of an angiosperm.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Cycas, the small specialised coralloid roots are associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation: The coralloid roots of Cycas house nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria. The fungal association called mycorrhiza belongs to Pinus, so it is the key trap here.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A taxonomist cannot decide whether two plant populations belong to the same species. She compares their chromosome number, chromosome structure and chromosome behaviour during cell division. Which approach to classification is she using?
questions.explanation: Cytotaxonomy uses cytological information such as chromosome number, structure and behaviour to resolve taxonomic confusion. Chemotaxonomy relies on the chemical constituents of the plant, not on chromosomes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In pteridophytes, the dominant phase of the life cycle is the diploid sporophyte, which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves.
Statement II: In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes are small but free-living, like the prothallus of ferns.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct because pteridophytes have a dominant, vascular sporophyte. Statement II is incorrect because gymnosperm gametophytes have no independent existence. They remain within the sporangia on the sporophyte, unlike the free-living fern prothallus.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fusion of two motile gametes which are dissimilar in size is termed as
questions.explanation: Anisogamy is the fusion of two gametes that differ in size. In oogamy, by contrast, a large non-motile female gamete fuses with a small motile male gamete.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q2)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Agar is used to grow microbes in the laboratory and to make ice-creams and jellies. From which pair of algae is it commercially obtained?
questions.explanation: Agar is a commercial product of the red algae Gelidium and Gracilaria. Laminaria, Sargassum, Fucus and Dictyota are brown algae, and Ulothrix and Volvox are green algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In some pteridophytes, the female gametophyte is retained on the parent sporophyte for variable periods, and the zygote develops into a young embryo within it; this is regarded as a precursor to the seed habit.
Statement II: This retention of the female gametophyte is characteristic of homosporous ferns such as Dryopteris.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Retention of the female gametophyte, with embryo development inside it, occurs in heterosporous genera such as Selaginella and Salvinia, where megaspores give rise to female gametophytes. Homosporous ferns like Dryopteris form free-living prothalli instead, so Statement II is false.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the ovule of a gymnosperm, the megaspore mother cell differentiates from which tissue?
options: A cell of the protective envelope (integument)
A cell of the pollen tube
questions.explanation: The megaspore mother cell arises from one of the cells of the nucellus. The envelopes only protect the nucellus, and together the two form the ovule.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Cyanobacteria, also called blue green algae, are no longer treated as algae under Kingdom Plantae.
Reason (R): Cyanobacteria are chlorophyll-bearing autotrophic organisms.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic autotrophs, so R is true. However, they were removed from Plantae because they are members of Monera, not because they photosynthesise, so R does not explain A. Being chlorophyll-bearing autotrophs is in fact a trait they share with true algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about bryophytes are correct?
(a) Mosses, along with lichens, are among the first organisms to colonise bare rocks.
(b) Mosses decompose rocks, making the substrate suitable for higher plants.
(c) Dense mats of mosses reduce the impact of falling rain and prevent soil erosion.
(d) Bryophytes in general are of great economic importance.
(e) Some mosses provide food for herbaceous mammals and birds.
questions.explanation: Statements (a), (b), (c) and (e) agree with NCERT, so four are correct. Statement (d) is wrong because bryophytes in general are of little economic importance, even though they matter a great deal ecologically.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the kingdoms in Whittaker's (1969) five kingdom classification?
questions.explanation: Whittaker's five kingdoms are Monera, Protista, Fungi, Animalia and Plantae. Archaea is not a kingdom in this system.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Besides their usual aquatic habitats, some algae live in association with animals. Which animal is cited in NCERT as an example?
questions.explanation: NCERT states that some algae occur in association with animals, for example on the sloth bear. Algae also associate with fungi to form lichens.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Cyanobacteria, also called blue-green algae, are no longer placed among the algae in Kingdom Plantae.
Statement II: The classification of flowering plants given by George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker is an artificial system based mainly on androecium structure.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Monera, including cyanobacteria, have been excluded from Plantae, so they are no longer treated as algae. Bentham and Hooker gave a natural system; the artificial system based on androecium structure was given by Linnaeus.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Cycas, small specialised roots called coralloid roots are associated with which of the following?
options: Mycorrhizal fungi that help in phosphate absorption
Nitrogen-fixing Rhizobium bacteria in root nodules
questions.explanation: The coralloid roots of Cycas house $N_2$-fixing cyanobacteria. The fungal association called mycorrhiza is the feature of Pinus, not Cycas, which makes option 1 a common trap.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following brown algae has a simple, branched, filamentous body rather than a profusely branched massive one?
questions.explanation: Ectocarpus is the simple branched filamentous member of Phaeophyceae. Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus have larger, more complex thalli, and kelps such as Laminaria can be massive.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Small leaves called microphylls are characteristic of which of the following pteridophytes?
questions.explanation: Selaginella bears small leaves (microphylls). Dryopteris, Adiantum and Pteris are ferns, and ferns have large leaves (macrophylls).
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct for Rhodophyceae?
(i) Most members are marine, with greater concentrations in warmer areas.
(ii) They are restricted to well-lighted regions close to the water surface.
(iii) Asexual reproduction occurs by non-motile spores.
(iv) Sexual reproduction is isogamous.
(v) Sexual reproduction is followed by complex post-fertilisation developments.
(vi) They possess chlorophyll a and d.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (iii), (v) and (vi) are correct, giving four. Red algae also occur at great depths where little light penetrates, so (ii) is wrong. Their sexual reproduction is oogamous, not isogamous, so (iv) is wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The term 'gymnosperm' means 'naked seed'. This name reflects which feature of these plants?
options: The ovules lack integuments, so the nucellus is directly exposed
The ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall, either before or after fertilisation
The seeds are enclosed in a fruit that splits open at maturity
The seeds lack an embryo and food reserves
questions.explanation: In gymnosperms the ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall, so they stay exposed both before and after fertilisation, and the seeds formed are uncovered. The nucellus is still protected by envelopes, which makes option 1 wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The thallus of Marchantia is dorsiventral and lies closely appressed to the substrate.
Statement II: The leafy gametophyte of a moss is attached to the soil by unicellular, unbranched rhizoids.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: The liverwort thallus is indeed dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate. The leafy stage of mosses, however, is anchored by multicellular, branched rhizoids, so Statement II is wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In members of Rhodophyceae, food is stored as:
options: Starch in pyrenoids along with protein
questions.explanation: Red algae store floridean starch, which is structurally very similar to amylopectin and glycogen. Laminarin and mannitol are the stored foods of brown algae, and pyrenoids with starch and protein are typical of green algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Algin
(b) Carrageen
(c) Floridean starch
(d) Laminarin
List-II
(i) Stored food of brown algae
(ii) Hydrocolloid obtained commercially from red algae
(iii) Gelatinous coating on the outside of brown algal cell walls
(iv) Reserve food of red algae, structurally similar to amylopectin and glycogen
questions.explanation: Algin coats brown algal cell walls and is a brown-algal hydrocolloid. Carrageen is a red-algal hydrocolloid, floridean starch is the red-algal reserve food, and laminarin is a brown-algal reserve food. The common trap is to treat algin as a stored food.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: An alga stores food as mannitol and produces pyriform gametes with two laterally attached flagella. Which other feature would you expect to find in this alga?
options: Chlorophyll a and b, with pyrenoids containing starch and protein
A cell wall containing cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters
Flagella 2–8 in number, equal and apically inserted
Chlorophyll a and c along with fucoxanthin, and a cellulosic wall coated with algin
questions.explanation: Mannitol storage and pear-shaped gametes with lateral flagella identify a brown alga, which has chlorophyll a, c, fucoxanthin and an algin-coated cellulose wall. Options 1 and 3 describe green algae, and option 2 describes the red-algal cell wall.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: The classification of flowering plants given by George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker was an artificial system based mainly on the structure of the androecium.
Statement II: Natural classification systems consider internal features such as anatomy, embryology and phytochemistry in addition to external features.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: The artificial system based on the androecium was given by Linnaeus. Bentham and Hooker gave a natural classification, which uses internal features like ultrastructure, anatomy, embryology and phytochemistry.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II for gymnosperms.
List-I
(A) Pollen grain
(B) Ovule
(C) Female gametophyte
(D) Megasporophyll
List-II
(I) Bears two or more archegonia
(II) Nucellus together with its protective envelopes
(III) Reduced male gametophyte
(IV) Bears ovules and may cluster to form female cones
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: The pollen grain is the reduced male gametophyte, and the ovule is the nucellus enclosed in envelopes. The multicellular female gametophyte bears two or more archegonia, and megasporophylls carry the ovules, often clustering into female cones.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(a) Algin
(b) Agar
(c) Chlorella
(d) Peat
List-II
(i) Sphagnum
(ii) Brown algae
(iii) Gelidium
(iv) Protein-rich food supplement used by space travellers
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Algin is a hydrocolloid from brown algae, and agar comes from Gelidium and Gracilaria. Chlorella is a protein-rich unicellular alga used as a food supplement, and peat is obtained from the moss Sphagnum.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following algae show oogamous sexual reproduction?
Volvox, Spirogyra, Fucus, Eudorina, Ulothrix, Polysiphonia
questions.explanation: Three of these are oogamous: Volvox, Fucus and Polysiphonia (red algae are always oogamous). Spirogyra and Ulothrix are isogamous, and Eudorina is anisogamous.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Gemmae
B. Primary protonema
C. Leafy stage of moss
D. Capsule
List-II
I. Site where spores are formed after meiosis
II. Develops directly from a spore
III. Asexual buds in receptacles on the liverwort thallus
IV. Bears the sex organs in mosses
Choose the correct answer:
questions.explanation: Gemmae are asexual buds in gemma cups, and the protonema arises directly from the spore. The leafy stage carries the antheridia and archegonia, and meiosis in the capsule produces the spores.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (green alga) with List-II (nature of gametes) and choose the correct option.
List-I
(a) Ulothrix
(b) Spirogyra
(c) Eudorina
(d) Volvox
List-II
(i) Non-flagellated gametes of similar size
(ii) Large non-motile female gamete and smaller motile male gamete
(iii) Flagellated gametes of similar size
(iv) Gametes dissimilar in size
questions.explanation: Ulothrix is isogamous with flagellated gametes, while Spirogyra is isogamous with non-flagellated gametes. Eudorina is anisogamous, and Volvox is oogamous. Students often swap Ulothrix and Spirogyra because both are isogamous.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous, producing large megaspores and small microspores.
Statement II: In heterosporous pteridophytes, the megaspores germinate to form male gametophytes and the microspores form female gametophytes.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores. Statement II reverses the roles, because megaspores give rise to female gametophytes and microspores give rise to male gametophytes.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following pteridophytes are heterosporous?
Selaginella, Salvinia, Pteris, Lycopodium, Adiantum, Equisetum
questions.explanation: Only Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores. The others are homosporous, like the majority of pteridophytes. Lycopodium is a trap because it shares the class Lycopsida with Selaginella.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a typical brown alga, the leaf-like photosynthetic organ of the plant body is called the:
questions.explanation: The brown-algal body has three parts. The holdfast attaches it to the substratum, the stipe is the stalk, and the frond is the leaf-like photosynthetic organ.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Porphyra, Laminaria and Sargassum, all of which are used as food, belong to the brown algae.
Statement II: Agar is used in the preparation of ice-creams and jellies.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: All three genera are among the marine algae used as food, but Porphyra is a red alga (Rhodophyceae), so Statement I is wrong. Statement II is correct.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the life cycle of a moss, the leafy stage develops:
options: From the foot of the sporophyte
As a lateral bud from the secondary protonema
From a gemma produced in a gemma cup
questions.explanation: The protonema develops directly from the spore. The leafy stage then arises as a lateral bud on the secondary protonema. Growth directly from the spore is true of the protonema, not of the leafy stage.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In Pinus, the male and female cones are borne on the same tree.
Statement II: In Cycas, the male cones and the megasporophylls are also borne on the same tree.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Pinus bears male and female cones on the same tree. Cycas is the contrasting case, with male cones and megasporophylls borne on different trees.
