questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (commercial product or use) with List-II (source) and choose the correct option.
List-I
(A) Algin
(B) Carrageen
(C) Agar
(D) Protein-rich food supplement used by space travellers
List-II
(I) Chlorella
(II) Gelidium
(III) Brown algae
(IV) Red algae
questions.explanation: Algin is a hydrocolloid of brown algae and carrageen comes from red algae. Agar is obtained from Gelidium (and Gracilaria), and the unicellular Chlorella is used as a protein-rich supplement. Swapping algin and carrageen is the usual trap.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the economic importance of algae is INCORRECT?
options: Algae increase the level of dissolved oxygen in their immediate environment.
Algin is a hydrocolloid obtained from red algae such as Gelidium.
Many species of Porphyra are used as food.
Agar is used in the preparation of ice-creams and jellies.
questions.explanation: Algin is produced by brown algae. Gelidium is a red alga and is a source of agar, not algin. The other three statements agree with NCERT.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following plants are heterosporous?
Selaginella, Salvinia, Equisetum, Dryopteris, Pinus, Cycas, Adiantum
questions.explanation: Among pteridophytes, Selaginella and Salvinia produce microspores and megaspores. All gymnosperms, including Pinus and Cycas, are also heterosporous. That gives four. Equisetum, Dryopteris and Adiantum are homosporous; the trap is forgetting that gymnosperms count too.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The prothallus of a fern is best described as:
options: A diploid, dependent sporophyte attached to the gametophyte
A haploid, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte
A compact cone of sporophylls bearing sporangia
A diploid structure formed directly from the zygote
questions.explanation: Spores germinate to form the prothallus. It is a small, multicellular, free-living, mostly photosynthetic thalloid gametophyte, so it is haploid. A compact cone of sporophylls is a strobilus, not a prothallus.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Numerical taxonomy
(b) Cytotaxonomy
(c) Chemotaxonomy
(d) Artificial system
List-II
(i) Chromosome number, structure and behaviour
(ii) A few superficial morphological characters
(iii) All observable characters coded and given equal importance
(iv) Chemical constituents of the plant
questions.explanation: Numerical taxonomy codes all observable characters and gives each equal weight. Cytotaxonomy uses cytological data and chemotaxonomy uses chemical constituents. Artificial systems relied on a few gross morphological features.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student argues: 'Since the main plant body of a bryophyte produces gametes, it must produce them by meiosis, as animals do.' Which of the following best corrects the student?
options: The gametophyte is diploid, and meiosis in it produces haploid antherozoids and eggs.
The zygote undergoes meiosis directly to form a new haploid gametophyte, so gametes need no reduction division.
The gametophyte is already haploid, so its gametes are formed without meiosis; meiosis occurs only in some cells of the sporophyte to form spores.
Meiosis occurs in the archegonium to form the egg, but antherozoids are formed without meiosis.
questions.explanation: Because the bryophyte gametophyte is haploid, the gametes it produces do not require reduction division. In this life cycle, meiosis happens in the diploid sporophyte, where it produces haploid spores.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A Prothallus is
options: A structure in pteridophytes formed before the thallus develops
A sporophytic free living structure formed in pteridophytes
A gametophyte free living structure formed in pteridophytes
A primitive structure formed after fertilization in pteridophytes
questions.explanation: In pteridophytes, a germinating spore gives rise to a small, inconspicuous, free-living, mostly photosynthetic gametophyte called the prothallus. This prothallus bears the sex organs.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q5)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are considered in a natural system of classification, as described in NCERT?
(i) External features
(ii) Ultrastructure
(iii) Anatomy
(iv) Embryology
(v) Phytochemistry
(vi) Assigning numbers and codes to characters and processing the data by computer
questions.explanation: Natural systems consider external features along with internal features such as ultrastructure, anatomy, embryology and phytochemistry, which makes five items. Coding characters and processing them by computer describes numerical taxonomy, not the natural system.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs of a commercially used hydrocolloid and its algal source is correctly matched?
questions.explanation: Carrageen is obtained from red algae and algin from brown algae. Agar comes from Gelidium and Gracilaria, which are red algae, not from the brown alga Laminaria.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the life cycle of a bryophyte, which of the following pairs consists ONLY of diploid cells?
options: Zygote and a sporophyte cell that undergoes meiosis
Egg and a cell of the sporophyte
questions.explanation: The zygote and every cell of the sporophyte derived from it, including the cells that undergo meiosis, are diploid (2n). Antherozoids, eggs, rhizoids and spores belong to the haploid phase, so each of the other options contains a haploid cell.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (classification approach) with List-II (its basis).
List-I
A. System of Linnaeus
B. System of Bentham and Hooker
C. Phylogenetic system
D. Numerical taxonomy
List-II
(i) Assumes that organisms of the same taxon share a common ancestor
(ii) Assigns codes to all observable characters and gives each character equal importance
(iii) Relies on gross morphology and the structure of the androecium
(iv) Uses natural affinities, including internal features such as embryology and phytochemistry
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Linnaeus gave an artificial system based on superficial characters and androecium structure. Bentham and Hooker gave a natural system that also uses internal features. Phylogenetic systems rest on evolutionary relationships and common ancestry, while numerical taxonomy codes all observable characters with equal weight. The usual trap is swapping C and D, because both use many sources of data.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A student observes a freshwater, unbranched filamentous alga under the microscope. Its cells have spiral, ribbon-shaped chloroplasts with pyrenoids, and a cellulose–pectose wall. During sexual reproduction, two non-flagellated gametes of similar size fuse. The alga is most likely:
questions.explanation: Ribbon-shaped chloroplasts with pyrenoids, a cellulose–pectose wall and isogamy with non-motile gametes identify the green alga Spirogyra. Ulothrix is ruled out because its gametes are flagellated. Ectocarpus is a brown alga with biflagellate gametes, and Polysiphonia is a red alga that is oogamous and stores floridean starch.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Phaeophyceae is incorrect?
options: Kelps are profusely branched forms that may reach a height of about 100 metres
In oogamous species, the union of gametes may take place within the oogonium
Brown algae are exclusively marine, with no freshwater representatives
The protoplast contains a centrally located vacuole and nucleus in addition to plastids
questions.explanation: Brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats, but Table 3.1 also lists rare freshwater and brackish-water forms, so 'exclusively marine' is wrong. The other three statements match NCERT.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which feature is shared by Selaginella and Pinus but is absent in Dryopteris?
options: Dominant sporophytic plant body with vascular tissues
Presence of archegonia as female sex organs
Production of two kinds of spores (heterospory)
questions.explanation: Selaginella (a heterosporous pteridophyte) and Pinus (a gymnosperm) both produce microspores and megaspores, whereas the fern Dryopteris is homosporous. All three have a vascular, dominant sporophyte and bear archegonia, while seeds are found only in Pinus.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fungal association with roots in the form of mycorrhiza is a characteristic example seen in which gymnosperm?
questions.explanation: NCERT cites Pinus as the gymnosperm whose roots form mycorrhiza with fungi. Cycas instead has coralloid roots with cyanobacteria, and Selaginella is a pteridophyte, not a gymnosperm.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Species of Sphagnum provide peat that is used as packing material for trans-shipment of living material. This use is mainly due to Sphagnum's:
options: rigid lignified tissues that resist crushing
questions.explanation: Sphagnum peat holds water well, so it keeps living material moist during transport. Bryophytes lack lignified vascular tissue, so option 4 is wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The rigid cell wall of a typical green alga is made of:
options: An inner layer of pectose and an outer layer of cellulose
An inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose
Cellulose covered by a gelatinous coating of algin
questions.explanation: Green algae have an inner cellulose layer and an outer pectose layer. The common trap is reversing the two layers. An algin coating is typical of brown algae, and polysulphate esters occur in red algal walls.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about gymnosperms is correct?
options: Pinus bears coralloid roots associated with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria
In Cycas, male cones and megasporophylls are borne on the same tree
Cycas has small specialised coralloid roots associated with $N_2$-fixing cyanobacteria
The ovules of gymnosperms are enclosed within an ovary wall before fertilisation
questions.explanation: Coralloid roots with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria are characteristic of Cycas. Pinus instead shows mycorrhizal (fungal) association. Cycas is dioecious, and gymnosperm ovules are always naked.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In Marchantia, gemmae are best described as:
options: Haploid unicellular spores formed by meiosis inside the capsule
Green, multicellular asexual buds that develop in gemma cups on the thallus
Diploid multicellular buds that grow on the seta of the sporophyte
Flagellated male gametes released from the antheridia
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds formed in small receptacles called gemma cups on the gametophytic thallus. They detach and grow into new plants. They are not spores, and they are not produced by meiosis or by the sporophyte.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) Algae lower the dissolved oxygen in their immediate surroundings.
(ii) Sargassum is among the marine algae used as food.
(iii) Algin is a water-holding substance produced by brown algae.
(iv) Chlorella is a multicellular, filamentous alga used as a food supplement.
(v) Gracilaria is a source of agar.
questions.explanation: Statements (ii), (iii) and (v) are correct. Statement (i) is wrong because photosynthesis raises dissolved oxygen. Statement (iv) is wrong because Chlorella is unicellular.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following correctly distinguishes oogamy from anisogamy as described in NCERT?
options: In oogamy the two gametes are similar in size, whereas in anisogamy they differ in size
In oogamy the female gamete is large and non-motile and the male gamete is small and motile, whereas anisogamy only involves gametes dissimilar in size
In oogamy both gametes are non-motile, whereas in anisogamy both gametes are always non-motile but unequal
Oogamy occurs only in colonial algae, whereas anisogamy occurs only in filamentous algae
questions.explanation: Anisogamy, as in Eudorina, is simply the fusion of gametes dissimilar in size. Oogamy, as in Volvox and Fucus, specifically involves a large static female gamete and a smaller motile male gamete. Fucus is neither colonial nor restricted to one form type, so option 4 fails.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about algae is incorrect?
options: Some algae grow on moist stones, soils and wood
Some algae live in association with fungi, forming lichens
Cyanobacteria are classified as algae because they are called blue green algae
A few marine algae, such as kelps, form massive plant bodies
questions.explanation: Members of Monera having cell walls, including cyanobacteria, have been excluded from Plantae. Despite the name 'blue green algae', they are no longer considered algae. The other statements agree with NCERT.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (alga) with List-II (type of sexual reproduction):
List-I
A. Ulothrix
B. Spirogyra
C. Eudorina
D. Fucus
List-II
I. Fusion of gametes dissimilar in size
II. Fusion of a large non-motile female gamete with a small motile male gamete
III. Fusion of flagellated gametes similar in size
IV. Fusion of non-flagellated gametes similar in size
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: Ulothrix has flagellated isogametes, while Spirogyra has non-flagellated isogametes. Eudorina is anisogamous and Fucus is oogamous. The usual trap is swapping the two isogamous genera.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In gymnosperms, the pollen grain represents which of the following?
options: A highly reduced male gametophyte confined to a few cells
A megaspore that has not yet germinated
questions.explanation: The microspore develops into a male gametophyte that is greatly reduced and has only a few cells, and this reduced structure is the pollen grain. Gymnosperm gametophytes are not free-living.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(a) Red algae lack flagella.
(b) The cell wall of red algae contains cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters.
(c) Brown algae possess chlorophyll a and c along with fucoxanthin.
(d) Green algae bear 2-8 equal, apically inserted flagella.
(e) Zoospores of brown algae are pear-shaped with two unequal, laterally attached flagella.
(f) Floridean starch is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure.
(g) Sexual reproduction in red algae is isogamous with simple post-fertilisation development.
questions.explanation: Statements (a) to (f) agree with NCERT, giving six correct statements. Statement (g) is wrong because sexual reproduction in red algae is oogamous and is followed by complex post-fertilisation developments.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following features are characteristic of Chlorophyceae?
• Dominance of chlorophyll a and b
• Food stored as floridean starch
• Pyrenoids located in chloroplasts
• Cell wall covered by a gelatinous coating of algin
• 2–8 equal, apically inserted flagella
• Fucoxanthin as the major accessory pigment
• Asexual reproduction by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia
questions.explanation: Four features belong to green algae: chlorophyll a and b, pyrenoids, 2–8 equal apical flagella, and zoospores formed in zoosporangia. Floridean starch is the red algal reserve, while an algin coating and fucoxanthin are brown algal features.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In green algae, the photosynthetic pigments are localised in definite chloroplasts.
Reason (R): Green algae, like the blue-green algae, lack membrane-bound organelles.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Green algae are eukaryotic plants whose pigments lie in chloroplasts of various shapes, so A is true. Only cyanobacteria (prokaryotes, no longer counted as algae) lack membrane-bound organelles, so R is false.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In gymnosperms, the pollen grain represents which of the following?
options: A highly reduced male gametophyte confined to a few cells
A male gamete that directly fuses with the egg
questions.explanation: Each microspore develops into a highly reduced male gametophyte of only a few cells, and this structure is the pollen grain. It is not itself a gamete, because the male gametes are carried within the pollen tube.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about reproduction in gymnosperms are correct?
(i) The megaspore mother cell divides meiotically to form four megaspores.
(ii) All four megaspores develop into female gametophytes within the ovule.
(iii) The female gametophyte is multicellular and bears two or more archegonia.
(iv) The female gametophyte is retained within the megasporangium.
(v) Pollen grains are carried to the ovules mainly by water.
(vi) After fertilisation, the ovules develop into seeds enclosed within fruits.
questions.explanation: Statements (i), (iii) and (iv) are correct. Only one megaspore develops into the female gametophyte, pollen is carried by air currents, and gymnosperm seeds are not covered by fruits, so (ii), (v) and (vi) are wrong.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The sporophyte of a bryophyte is not free-living.
Reason (R): The bryophyte sporophyte remains attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and derives nourishment from it.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The bryophyte sporophyte grows attached to the gametophyte and depends on it for nourishment. That dependence is exactly why it is not free-living, so R explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bryophytes are called the 'amphibians of the plant kingdom' because they:
options: live in soil but depend on water for sexual reproduction
live in water but carry out photosynthesis only on land
have a gametophyte that lives in water and a sporophyte that lives on land
lack vascular tissue and so absorb water through their whole surface
questions.explanation: Bryophytes grow on soil, but their antherozoids need water to reach the archegonium, so sexual reproduction depends on water. The other options invent habitat splits that NCERT does not describe.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Both Ulothrix and Spirogyra show isogamous sexual reproduction.
Statement II: The gametes of Spirogyra bear flagella and are motile.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation: Both genera fuse gametes of similar size, so both are isogamous. However, only Ulothrix gametes are flagellated, whereas Spirogyra gametes are non-flagellated and non-motile.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Algae are of paramount importance as primary producers in aquatic habitats.
Reason (R): Through photosynthesis, algae produce energy-rich compounds that form the basis of the food cycles of all aquatic animals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Algae are primary producers precisely because they photosynthetically make the energy-rich compounds on which aquatic food cycles depend. So R directly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In the life cycle of a moss such as Funaria, the leafy stage develops:
options: From the secondary protonema as a lateral bud
From the capsule of the sporophyte after meiosis
From a gemma detached from a gemma cup
questions.explanation: The protonema develops directly from the spore. The leafy stage then arises from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud. The common trap is thinking the spore gives rise to the leafy shoot directly.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Algae are found in many habitats besides water. In which of the following associations do algae occur together with fungi?
questions.explanation: A lichen is an association between an alga and a fungus. Mycorrhiza is a fungus–root association, as in Pinus. Coralloid roots of Cycas carry cyanobacteria, and cyanobacteria are no longer counted as algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are members of Phaeophyceae?
Ectocarpus, Porphyra, Dictyota, Gracilaria, Sargassum, Polysiphonia, Fucus, Laminaria
questions.explanation: Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Sargassum, Fucus and Laminaria are brown algae, giving five. Porphyra, Gracilaria and Polysiphonia are red algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bryophytes are called 'amphibians of the plant kingdom' because they:
options: live in soil but need water for sexual reproduction
have both a haploid and a diploid free-living phase
grow partly submerged in water and partly in air
can photosynthesise both on land and under the sea
questions.explanation: Bryophytes can live on land in soil, but their antherozoids must swim through water to reach the archegonium. They are not called amphibians because of their habitat or the alternation of free-living phases, since their sporophyte is not free-living.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Algin
B. Carrageen
C. Agar
D. Chlorella
List-II
(i) Protein-rich unicellular alga used as a food supplement by space travellers
(ii) Hydrocolloid obtained from red algae
(iii) Hydrocolloid obtained from brown algae
(iv) Product of Gelidium and Gracilaria used to grow microbes
Choose the correct answer.
questions.explanation: Algin is the hydrocolloid of brown algae and carrageen is the hydrocolloid of red algae. Agar comes from Gelidium and Gracilaria and is used as a culture medium for microbes. Chlorella is the protein-rich food supplement. The usual trap is swapping algin and carrageen.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In mosses, the leafy stage develops directly from the spore.
Reason (R): The protonema of a moss is a creeping, green, branched and frequently filamentous stage.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The spore germinates into the protonema, not the leafy stage, so A is false. The leafy stage arises later as a lateral bud on the secondary protonema. R correctly describes the protonema.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The sporophyte of mosses is more elaborate than that of liverworts.
Reason (R): The moss sporophyte is free-living and independent of the gametophyte for nutrition.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: The moss sporophyte is more elaborate than the liverwort sporophyte, and mosses also have an elaborate spore dispersal mechanism. However, in all bryophytes the sporophyte stays attached to the gametophyte and draws nourishment from it, so R is false.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which pair consists only of heterosporous pteridophytes?
questions.explanation: NCERT names Selaginella and Salvinia as heterosporous genera, since they produce both megaspores and microspores. Most other pteridophytes, including the ferns and Equisetum listed here, are homosporous.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the comparison of algal classes, the cell wall of red algae is made of:
options: An inner cellulose layer and an outer pectose layer only
questions.explanation: Rhodophyceae have cell walls of cellulose, pectin and polysulphate esters. Cellulose with algin is the brown-algal wall. An inner cellulose layer with outer pectose describes green algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about liverworts is correct?
options: The thallus of Marchantia is erect and radially symmetrical.
Gemmae are produced by meiosis inside the capsule.
Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds that develop in gemma cups on the thallus.
The sporophyte of a liverwort consists only of a capsule and lacks a foot and seta.
questions.explanation: Gemmae are green, multicellular asexual buds borne in gemma cups. The liverwort thallus is dorsiventral and closely appressed to the substrate. The sporophyte has a foot, seta and capsule, and meiosis in the capsule produces spores, not gemmae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (class) with List-II (example):
List-I
A. Psilopsida
B. Lycopsida
C. Sphenopsida
D. Pteropsida
List-II
(i) Equisetum
(ii) Adiantum
(iii) Psilotum
(iv) Lycopodium
Choose the correct option.
questions.explanation: The correct pairs are Psilopsida–Psilotum, Lycopsida–Lycopodium, Sphenopsida–Equisetum and Pteropsida–Adiantum (a fern). The usual trap is mixing up Psilotum and Lycopodium.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Four algae P, Q, R and S show the following features of their fusing gametes:
P: both gametes flagellated and similar in size
Q: both gametes non-flagellated and similar in size
R: both gametes motile but dissimilar in size
S: a large static female gamete and a small motile male gamete
Which option correctly gives the type of sexual reproduction and a matching example for each?
options: P – isogamy (Ulothrix); Q – anisogamy (Spirogyra); R – anisogamy (Eudorina); S – oogamy (Fucus)
P – isogamy (Ulothrix); Q – isogamy (Spirogyra); R – anisogamy (Eudorina); S – oogamy (Volvox)
P – isogamy (Spirogyra); Q – isogamy (Ulothrix); R – oogamy (Eudorina); S – anisogamy (Volvox)
P – anisogamy (Ulothrix); Q – isogamy (Spirogyra); R – oogamy (Fucus); S – oogamy (Volvox)
questions.explanation: Gametes of similar size give isogamy, whether flagellated (Ulothrix) or not (Spirogyra). Gametes of unequal size give anisogamy (Eudorina). A large static egg fusing with a small motile male gamete is oogamy (Volvox, Fucus). The trap is calling Q anisogamous just because its gametes are non-motile.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: In mosses, the sporophyte is free-living and independent of the gametophyte for its nutrition.
Statement II: In mosses, the leafy stage develops from the secondary protonema as a lateral bud.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect: in bryophytes the sporophyte remains attached to the photosynthetic gametophyte and draws nourishment from it. Statement II is correct: the leafy gametophore arises as a lateral bud from the secondary protonema.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a gymnosperm such as Pinus, which of the following pairs consists of structures that are BOTH haploid?
questions.explanation: The female gametophyte develops from a haploid megaspore, and the pollen grain is the male gametophyte from a haploid microspore, so both are haploid. The nucellus, the sporophylls and the zygote are diploid structures of the sporophyte generation.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(a) Algin
(b) Floridean starch
(c) Agar
(d) Laminarin
List-II
(i) Reserve food of red algae, structurally similar to amylopectin and glycogen
(ii) Commercial product of Gelidium and Gracilaria used to grow microbes
(iii) Complex carbohydrate stored as food in brown algae
(iv) Hydrocolloid forming the gelatinous coating on brown algal cell walls
Choose the correct option:
questions.explanation: Algin coats brown-algal walls, floridean starch is the red-algal reserve, agar comes from Gelidium and Gracilaria, and laminarin is a brown-algal storage carbohydrate. The trap is swapping algin and laminarin, since both belong to brown algae.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A plant shows thallus level of organization. It shows rhizoids and is haploid. It needs water to complete its life cycle because the male gametes are motile. Identify the group to which it belongs to
questions.explanation: Bryophytes have a thalloid body attached by rhizoids, and their dominant plant body is the haploid gametophyte. They also need water for their motile antherozoids to reach the egg.
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 11, Ch 3 (MCQ Q4)
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Conifers are able to withstand dry and windy conditions with relatively little water loss.
Reason (R): Their needle-like leaves have a reduced surface area, a thick cuticle and sunken stomata.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Gymnosperm leaves are adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. In conifers, the small surface area of needles, the thick cuticle and the sunken stomata together reduce water loss, so R directly explains A.
questions.basis: NCERT Class 11 Biology, Ch 3 · Plant Kingdom
